question.problem:
The area of ​​the triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $24\sqrt{2} \text{ cm}^2.$ Find $AB.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226856/assets/e93e732bd04cfda304c2098087548a638d8d869ccf8b1050235e8207825875d3.png)
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
\mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}bc\sin{A},
$$

where $\angle{A}$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB, \\ b & =AC=12\text{ cm}, \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\sin{45^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $c=AB,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 24\sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 12\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\ 24\sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 12\cdot c\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ 24\cancel{\sqrt{2}} & =3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}c \\ 24 & =3c \\ c & =8\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AB = 8\,\textrm{cm}.$
